literal_meaning: ধোপা এবং নাপিতের সেবা বন্ধ করা (to boycott the services of the washerman and barber)
figurative_meaning_bn: সমাজচ্যুত করা বা সামাজিক দণ্ড দেওয়া
figurative_meaning_en: To socially ostracize or impose social punishment
similar_in_english: To give someone the cold shoulder
example_sentences_in_bangla: গ্রামের লোকেরা তার অপরাধের জন্য ধোপা-নাপিত বন্ধ করেছে।
সমাজ থেকে বহিষ্কৃত হওয়ার জন্য তারা ধোপা-নাপিত বন্ধ করল।
example_sentences_in_english: The villagers imposed a dhopa-napit boycott on him for his offense.
They ostracized him from society by closing off the washerman and barber services.
history: This idiom originates from traditional Bengali village panchayat systems, where social offenses were punished by boycotting essential services like those of the washerman (dhopa) and barber (napit), effectively isolating the offender from community life.
note: The idiom reflects pre-modern rural social control mechanisms in Bengal.
